claims.text: The mapping review included 114 machine-knit sensor manuscripts after screening.
Stretch/strain sensors were the most common sensor type in the review (53 manuscripts; 46.5%).
The review reports that 32 studies (28.1%) integrated sensors directly into a full garment, while 67 (58.8%) reported no garment integration.
The authors recommend reporting yarn composition/manufacturer, knitting-machine model and settings such as gauge, and ideally knitting instructions or machine files to support replication.

The review identifies limited comparison against common wearables and no randomized controlled trials among the reviewed studies, and calls for better accuracy validation and collaboration with HCI and fashion experts.

limitations: Secondary mapping review; not a primary sensor prototype or authoring-tool study.
The database search ended on 2023-10-31, so the review does not represent later publications.
Bibliographic publication details in the supplied PDF remain unresolved; figures and counts are reported as the review's findings, not independently re-extracted across all 114 papers.
coding.relevanceToStudio: Useful background for the review taxonomy and for documenting material, machine, gauge and fabrication-file provenance. Its recommendations are research context, not validated requirements or performance claims for Soft Sensor Studio.
